method: Each weekly snapshot's ranked candidates form an equal-weighted research basket per category, bought at the as-of close and held for 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. Returns are PRICE returns (dividends excluded) minus the category's assumed friction on entry and exit, compared with the category benchmark over the same days. A candidate whose prices stop (delisting, ticker change) is reported as 'return unavailable' and counted in a separate column, never silently dropped; delisting returns are not available from the data sources. Turnover is the share of a category's names that changed from the previous week. No edge is claimed before at least 52 weekly snapshots exist, and none is claimed afterwards without a statistical test.

measurement_revision.rule: Every stock and its benchmark are measured between the same two NYSE sessions: the snapshot's as-of close and exactly N sessions later (TRACK_HORIZONS). A horizon is pending until that session has passed and its closes are published. A missing entry or exit close is reported as missing, never bridged to another session. A basket counts as complete only when every published pick and the benchmark have both closes; incomplete baskets are shown with their measurable count and left out of the completed-basket averages. Summaries, turnover and weekly chains are computed separately for each methodology version. Prices pass the same validation as ranking (PRICE_BAR_RULE, including the close-verified end-of-session quote bar when the history file lags).
measurement_revision.previous: Before 2026-11-04 the tracking file used unvalidated provider history, positional session counts and category aggregates across versions. No 1-, 3-, 6- or 12-month result had completed under it.

limitations: Price returns only: dividends are excluded, which understates returns of dividend payers and benchmarks.
Delisting returns are not available from the data sources; affected names are listed as unavailable.
Friction is an assumption (bps per side), not measured execution cost.

decision_desk.method: Ratings stored in a weekly snapshot are tracked like the lists: price return from the as-of close over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months minus the entry's benchmark over the same sessions, before costs and dividends, averaged by rating. Ratings computed when the site is built from an older snapshot are previews and are never tracked. No edge is claimed before MIN_SNAPSHOTS_FOR_EVIDENCE snapshots.
